newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAPAN CONDO MARKET SLOW IN JULY - RESEARCH BODY.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN CONDO MARKET SLOW IN JULY - RESEARCH BODY.

text.p: Japan's Real Estate Economic Institute said on Monday the number of new condominiums put up for sale in the Tokyo and Osaka areas fell in July and their actual sales were slow as well.
The private research institute said that a total of 7,147 condominiums were put up for sale in the Tokyo metropolitan area in July, down 28.9 precent from a year ago.
Of them, 5,211 condominiums, or 72.9 percent, were sold in July, it said. They were sold for 42.8 million yen per unit, down 430,000 yen from a year ago, it said.
In July last year, 83.5 percent of the new condominiums were sold.
In the Osaka area in July, 4,165 new condominiums were put up for sale, down 21.0 percent, the research institute said.
Of them, 3,029 units, or 72.7 percent, were sold in July, it said. In July last year, 80.1 percent of the new condominiums were sold, it said.
They were sold for 37.6 million yen per unit, up 1.31 million yen from a year ago, it said.
